definition_zh: 极小的；微小的；细小的；微不足道的
definition_en: extremely small in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 掌心上一粒几乎看不见的小沙，得眯起眼才分得清
scene: 雨后的石阶上，一只小生物正慢慢横着爬。A tiny crab crossed the wet step and disappeared into a crack.
sceneCN: 这里 tiny 是「极小的」（第 1 个义项：体积非常小）；句意为一只极小的蟹爬过湿石阶，钻进石缝不见了。画面有水光、石阶与一条细缝。

pos.zh: 形容词：极小的；微小的；细小的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；极小」
形容词比较级，义为「更小的」
形容词最高级，义为「最小的」

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: very small indeed in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 体积确实非常小
senses.example: A tiny insect landed on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一只极小的虫子落在书页上。
senses.why: The word is probably a northern form related to little, with the ending shaping a diminutive.
senses.whyCN: 本词很可能是与 little 相关的北方方言形式，词尾带有「小」的意味。

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: very small in quantity or degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上非常小
senses.example: Only a tiny amount of salt is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 只需要极少一点盐。
senses.why: The size sense transfers to quantity: a small amount is measured on the same scale as a small object.
senses.whyCN: 大小义转到数量上：少量与小的物体用同一把尺子衡量。

senses.title: Small and endearing
senses.definition: small in a way that makes people fond
senses.definitionCN: 小得让人心生喜爱
senses.example: She bought a tiny pair of boots for the doll.
senses.exampleCN: 她给娃娃买了一双小小的靴子。
senses.why: Smallness plus care gives the affectionate tone the word often carries.
senses.whyCN: 细小的体积配上用心，本词常带着亲昵的口气。

senses.title: Small in importance
senses.definition: of very little importance or significance
senses.definitionCN: 重要性或意义很小
senses.example: The differences between the two drafts were tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 两份草稿之间的差别微乎其微。
senses.why: If physical size is near zero, importance measured the same way is also near zero.
senses.whyCN: 若体积近乎零，用同一把尺子衡量的重要性也近乎零。

senses.title: A tiny fraction
senses.definition: a very small proportion of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体中一个非常小的份额
senses.example: A tiny fraction of the budget went to repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中极小一部分用于维修。
senses.why: A part cut small enough is described with the size word rather than a counting word.
senses.whyCN: 被切得足够小的一份，用大小词而非计数词来描述。

senses.title: The tiniest detail
senses.definition: the most minute element, in the superlative tiniest
senses.definitionCN: 最高级形式下指最细小的要素
senses.example: She noticed the tiniest change in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她发觉他声音里最细微的变化。
senses.why: Even a detail has a size, and at the smallest scale it becomes tiny.
senses.whyCN: 细节也有大小，到了最小尺度就成了 tiny。

senses.title: Small and young
senses.definition: used of a very young person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 形容年幼的人或动物
senses.example: The tiny kitten could not yet open its eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 那只幼小的猫还睁不开眼。
senses.why: Young bodies are small bodies, so age and size share the same word.
senses.whyCN: 幼小的身体就是小小的身体，年龄与大小共用一词。

senses.title: Small in comparison
senses.definition: small when set beside something much larger
senses.definitionCN: 与更大之物相比显得很小
senses.example: From the air the ship looked tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 从空中看去那艘船显得极小。
senses.why: The word often measures against a larger frame, making size relative rather than fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常相对更大的参照来衡量，因此大小是相对的。

intro.en: The adjective appears in the late sixteenth century, probably from a northern or British dialect form related to little, with a diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪末出现，很可能来自与 little 相关的地方方言形式，并带有表小的词尾。

items.en: A dialect form tine or tiney is recorded for little or small.
items.cn: 方言形式 tine、tiney 已有记载，意为「小的」。

items.en: Scholars connect it with little, but the exact path is not settled.
items.cn: 学者把它与 little 联系起来，但确切路径尚未定论。

items.en: Tiny is recorded in written English from the late sixteenth century.
items.cn: tiny 自十六世纪末见于书面英语。

items.en: The comparative tinier and the superlative tiniest stabilize by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 比较级 tinier 与最高级 tiniest 在十八世纪定型。

items.en: The word becomes the everyday strong form of small, warmer than minute.
items.cn: 本词成为 small 的日常强形式，比 minute 更带感情。

items.en: It spreads from physical size to amount, detail, and importance.
items.cn: 它从体积扩展到数量、细节与重要性。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other words ending in a similar shape, while the near-meaning group gathers the scale of smallness.
note.cn: 形近组列出结尾形状相似的其他词，近义组则聚集「小」的程度上的一组词。

entries.definitionCN: 叮当声；只是形近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the word's dialect origins, its scale, and the comparisons it invites.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从它的方言来源、尺度以及它引出的对比入手。

normal.en: Tiny is probably a dialect cousin of little, so the small meaning is built in.
normal.cn: tiny 很可能是 little 的方言近亲，小的意思天生带着。

normal.en: Tinier and tiniest follow the y to i rule: y becomes i before -er.
normal.cn: tinier 与 tiniest 遵守 y 变 i 的规则。

normal.en: A tiny bit is the everyday phrase for a very small quantity.
normal.cn: a tiny bit 是表示极少量的日常说法。

normal.en: The tiniest detail uses the superlative for the finest point.
normal.cn: the tiniest detail 用最高级表示最细微之处。

normal.en: Minute is formal, tiny is warm; huge is the exact opposite.
normal.cn: minute 偏正式，tiny 更亲切，huge 正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a pinhead with a whole insect balanced on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针的针头上落着一整只虫子。

abstract.en: Think of a ship seen from a plane window, no bigger than a speck.
abstract.cn: 想从机窗望见的一艘船，小得像一粒斑点。

abstract.en: A tiny thing demands that you lean closer, and leaning is the word's feeling.
abstract.cn: 微小之物逼你凑近，凑近正是这个词的感觉。

examples.en: A tiny bird was perched on the wire.
examples.cn: 一只极小的鸟停在电线上。

examples.en: Add a tiny bit of sugar to the sauce.
examples.cn: 在酱汁里加一点点糖。

examples.en: From the top of the hill the houses looked tiny.
examples.cn: 从山顶看去，那些房子显得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太迷你」——太迷你了，小得放在掌心都找不着。

root: 一般认为与 little 相关的方言形式 tiney 有关，词尾带表小色彩，确切来源不确定；十六世纪末进入书面英语。

sensesIntro.en: One scale of smallness runs through the entry: physical size first, then amount, affection, importance, fractions, details, young creatures, and size seen from far away.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条「小」的尺度贯穿全词：先体积，再到数量、亲昵、重要性、比例、细节、幼小以及远观的大小。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speck on the palm that you must squint to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心一粒得眯眼才看得见的尘点。

branches.en: Small bodies, including young ones.
branches.cn: 小的身体，包括幼小的个体。

branches.en: Smallness measured in quantity and proportion.
branches.cn: 以数量与比例衡量的小。

branches.en: The affectionate colour of the size.
Smallness of importance and of detail.
branches.cn: 重要性与细节上的微小。

branches.en: Small compared with a larger frame.
branches.cn: 与更大参照相比显出的小。

intro.en: The adjective takes the regular English endings for comparison and a noun, plus the y to i spelling change.
intro.cn: 这个形容词接常规英语的比较级与名词词尾，并遵守 y 变 i 的拼写规则。

latinIntro.en: Tiny has no Latin etymon; the Latin items below offer the formal scale of smallness for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: tiny 没有拉丁词源；下面的拉丁词提供正式语体的「小」尺度作对照。

items.example: The ending gives tiny its adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾让 tiny 成为形容词。

items.example: Tinier means even smaller.
Tiniest means the smallest.
Tininess names the quality.

items.meaning: y becomes i before a suffix
items.meaningCN: 后缀前 y 变 i
items.example: Tiniest drops the y for i.
items.exampleCN: tiniest 把 y 换成 i。

items.example: Tinish is not standard but would mean somewhat small.
items.exampleCN: tinish 不属标准词，但意为「有点小」。

items.example: Tiny has no common -ly adverb.
items.exampleCN: tiny 没有常用副词形式。

items.example: Semi-tiny is only a playful formation.

definition_zh: 疲倦；疲劳；使疲倦；厌倦；（美式）轮胎
definition_en: to become or make someone feel in need of rest; also to lose interest, and in American spelling a wheel covering of rubber
core_image: 一个人瘫在椅子上，眼皮沉得抬不起来
scene: 连续加了三天班，他连饭都不想吃。Two long shifts had tired him so much that he fell asleep at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 tire 是「使疲倦」（第 2 个义项：使人感到需要休息）；句意为连续两个长班让他累得在桌边睡着。画面有椅子、台灯与未动的碗筷。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词形容词化，义为「疲倦的」
由现在分词形容词化，义为「累人的」
加 -ness 构成，义为「疲倦」
加 -less 构成，义为「不知疲倦的」

senses.title: To become weary
senses.definition: to become in need of rest or sleep
senses.definitionCN: 变得需要休息或睡觉
senses.example: She tires quickly in the afternoon heat.
senses.exampleCN: 午后炎热中她很容易疲倦。
senses.why: The verb goes back to an Old English word for failing or giving out, and the body is what gives out first.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词源自古英语表示「疲乏、耗尽」的词，而最先耗尽的是身体。

senses.title: To make someone weary
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel in need of rest
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到需要休息
senses.example: Two long shifts had tired him completely.
senses.exampleCN: 连续两个长班让他彻底累垮。
senses.why: The same giving-out is now caused from outside, by work or effort.
senses.whyCN: 同样的耗尽此时由外部的劳作造成。

senses.title: To lose interest
senses.definition: to become bored with something, usually with of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物失去兴趣，常与 of 连用
senses.example: They never tire of watching the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从不厌倦看海。
senses.why: Interest also gives out with repetition, so the body's fatigue becomes mental boredom.
senses.whyCN: 兴趣也会因重复而耗尽，身体的疲乏于是变成心智的厌倦。

senses.title: A wheel covering
senses.definition: the rubber covering on a wheel, spelled tyre in British English
senses.definitionCN: 车轮上的橡胶外圈，英式拼作 tyre
senses.example: One tire was flat after the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶后一只轮胎瘪了。
senses.why: The tire is usually explained as a shortened form of attire, the wheel being dressed in rubber.
senses.whyCN: 轮胎一般被解释为 attire 的缩略，车轮「穿上」了橡胶。

senses.title: A spare wheel
senses.definition: a spare tire kept in a car for emergencies
senses.definitionCN: 车上备用的轮胎
senses.example: He changed to the spare tire by the roadside.
senses.exampleCN: 他在路边换上了备用轮胎。
senses.why: This is simply the wheel sense used in a fixed phrase about readiness.
senses.whyCN: 这只是轮胎义用在表示备用的固定短语中。

senses.title: To exhaust by effort
senses.definition: to exhaust someone through continued effort or strain
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续的劳作或压力使人耗尽
senses.example: The climb tired the whole group.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攀登把整队人都累坏了。
senses.why: Effort draws out strength until nothing is left, which is the older sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 费力把力气抽干，这正是动词较古的含义。

senses.title: A tire on a bicycle
senses.definition: the rubber outer part of a bicycle wheel
senses.definitionCN: 自行车轮上的橡胶外圈
senses.example: The rear tire needed more air.
senses.exampleCN: 后轮外胎需要再打点气。
senses.why: Any rubber wheel covering takes the word, whatever the vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 任何橡胶外包的车轮，不论何种车辆，都用这个词。

senses.title: Tire of waiting
senses.definition: to grow impatient with a delay
senses.definitionCN: 对拖延变得不耐烦
senses.example: The crowd began to tire of waiting at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在门口等得不耐烦了。
senses.why: Patience is also a strength that can give out, so delay tires the waiting person.
senses.whyCN: 耐心也是一种会耗尽的力气，所以拖延会让人疲倦。

intro.en: The verb is native and originally meant to fail or give out; the wheel noun is a separate and disputed story usually traced to attire.
intro.cn: 动词是本土词，本义为「疲乏、耗尽」；轮胎名词则是另一段有争议的来源，通常追溯到 attire。

items.en: The verb tierian meant to fail, grow faint, or give out.
items.cn: 动词 tierian 意为「疲乏、衰弱、耗尽」。

items.en: The sense narrows to physical and mental weariness.
items.cn: 词义收窄为身体与精神的疲倦。

items.en: The phrase tire of extends weariness to interest and patience.
items.cn: tire of 把疲倦扩展到兴趣与耐心上。

items.en: The noun tire for a wheel covering appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 表示轮胎的名词 tire 在十九世纪出现。

items.en: It is usually explained as a short form of attire, a wheel dressed in rubber.
items.cn: 一般解释为 attire 的缩略，即车轮「穿衣」为橡胶。

items.en: British spelling keeps tyre for the wheel, while American uses tire.
items.cn: 英式拼写保留 tyre 指轮胎，美式则用 tire。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word family and the British wheel spelling, and the near-meaning group lists weariness and wheel words.
note.cn: 形近组收集词族与英式轮胎拼写，近义组列出疲倦与车轮类词。

normal.en: Tire of means weary of, and the of points at the thing that wears you down.
normal.cn: tire of 意为厌倦，of 指向那个把你磨累的对象。

normal.en: Tired is the participle turned adjective, tiring is the other side of it.
normal.cn: tired 是分词作形容词，tiring 是它的另一面。

normal.en: Tire out strengthens the verb with out, meaning completely.
normal.cn: tire out 用 out 加强，意为彻底累垮。

normal.en: British tyre and American tire name the same rubber ring.
normal.cn: 英式 tyre 与美式 tire 指同一个橡胶圈。

normal.en: The wheel tire probably comes from attire, a wheel dressed for the road.
normal.cn: 轮胎义大概来自 attire，车轮为上路而穿衣。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that dims as the battery drains.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯随电池耗尽而变暗。

abstract.en: Think of lids that will not stay open at the end of a long day.
abstract.cn: 想漫长一天结束时怎么也撑不开的眼皮。

abstract.en: A tire on a car is a black ring keeping effort from wearing the wheel.
abstract.cn: 车胎是一只黑圈，让摩擦磨不到轮子。

examples.en: Long meetings tire me faster than hard work.
examples.cn: 长会比苦干更容易让我疲倦。

examples.en: He never tires of telling that story.
examples.cn: 他讲那个故事从不觉得腻。

examples.en: The front tire lost air on the rough road.
examples.cn: 前胎在颠簸的路上漏了气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太儿」——太儿戏了，跑来跑去累得不行。

root: 动词来自古英语 tierian（疲乏、耗尽），本土词；轮胎名词一般视为 attire（穿着）的缩略，来源尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The body's giving-out is the centre; from it come fatigue, exhaustion by effort, boredom with repetition, and impatience with waiting, while the wheel noun follows its own dressed-in-rubber story.
sensesIntro.cn: 身体的耗尽为核心；由此生出疲劳、劳作致疲、厌倦重复与等待不耐，而轮胎名词另走「穿上橡胶」的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength draining away until the body cannot move.
core.cn: 核心意象：力气一点点流走，身体动弹不得。

intro.cn: 疲倦动词与轮胎名词都接常规英语词尾，这是构词主线。

latinIntro.en: The verb has no Latin etymon; the Latin list gives near-synonyms for weariness.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词没有拉丁词源；拉丁表给出表示疲倦的近义词。

items.example: The root carries the whole fatigue sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载全部疲倦义。

items.example: Tired works as an adjective.
Tiring describes work that wears you out.
Tiredness names the state.
Tireless means never tiring.
Tiresome means tiresome or annoying.
Tire out means exhaust fully.
items.exampleCN: tire out 意为彻底累垮。

items.example: Tires is both a verb form and a wheel plural.
items.exampleCN: tires 既是动词形式也是轮胎复数。

definition_zh: 到；向；往；向……（表示方向）；给；对于；（不定式标记）
definition_en: a preposition of direction, destination, or receiver, and the marker placed before the basic form of a verb
core_image: 手指向一个方向，箭头正指着目的地
scene: 站台上的人都盯着远处那一点，等那列火车开过来。The crowd walked to the far end of the platform and waited.
sceneCN: 这里 to 是「往、到」（第 1 个义项：表示朝向或到达某处）；句意为人群走到站台尽头等着。画面有铁路、人群与远处车灯。

derivatives.zh: 加普通后缀 -ward 构成，义为「朝向」
toward 的英式变体，义为「朝向」
复合词，义为「在今天」
复合词，义为「今晚」

senses.title: Towards a place
senses.definition: in the direction of a place, with the idea of arrival
senses.definitionCN: 朝某地的方向，并含抵达之意
senses.example: They walked to the far end of the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走到站台的另一端。
senses.why: The Old English preposition named motion toward a goal, and the goal being reached is the arrival sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语介词表示朝目标移动，抵达目标便成了「到」的义。

senses.title: As far as
senses.definition: used to show the limit or end of a movement or range
senses.definitionCN: 表示移动或范围的终点
senses.example: The queue stretched from the gate to the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍从大门一直排到街角。
senses.why: Direction plus limit gives a line that ends at a point.
senses.whyCN: 方向加界限，画出一条终于某点的线。

senses.title: The receiver of an action
senses.definition: used to introduce the person who receives something
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出接受某物的人
senses.example: Please give the letter to your teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 请把信交给你的老师。
senses.why: The goal of a movement is often a person, so the reaching word becomes the receiving word.
senses.whyCN: 移动目标常是一个人，因此「抵达」的词也成了「给予」的词。

senses.title: Showing a relationship
senses.definition: used to show a relationship between two things, such as comparison or attitude
senses.definitionCN: 表示两事物之间的关系，如比较或态度
senses.example: She is kind to strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 她对陌生人很和善。
senses.why: The goal of an attitude is the person or thing it is directed at.
senses.whyCN: 态度的指向就是它所对着的人或物。

senses.title: Telling the time
senses.definition: used in clock readings before the next hour
senses.definitionCN: 钟点表达中用于下一个整点之前
senses.example: It is ten to six.
senses.exampleCN: 现在五点五十（差十分六点）。
senses.why: Counting forward toward the coming hour is the direction sense applied to the clock face.
senses.whyCN: 朝着下一个小时数下去，就是方向义用在钟面上。

senses.title: Before the basic verb
senses.definition: the marker used before the basic form of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词原形前的标记
senses.example: He wants to leave now.
senses.exampleCN: 他现在想走。
senses.why: The old preposition of direction was placed before a verb to show the intended action, and became the infinitive marker.
senses.whyCN: 古英语表示方向的介词被放在动词前表示打算做的动作，后来成为不定式标记。

senses.title: Showing purpose
senses.definition: used to state the purpose of an action
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明动作的目的
senses.example: She came to say goodbye.
senses.exampleCN: 她是来道别的。
senses.why: Reaching toward an aim is the same movement, now aimed at an act rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标抵达的同一动作，此时目标是个行为而非地点。

senses.title: Closed or shut
senses.definition: used with door in the phrase to after door to mean shut
senses.definitionCN: 与门连用，表示关严
senses.example: Pull the door to when you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开时把门带上。
senses.why: Something that has moved right up to its frame is wholly closed.
senses.whyCN: 完全抵到门框的东西就彻底关上了。

senses.title: To and fro
senses.definition: used in the phrase to and fro for back-and-forth movement
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 to and fro，表示来回移动
senses.example: The pendulum swung to and fro.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆来回摆动。
senses.why: Two opposite direction words paired give movement that never settles.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反方向的词配对，得到永远停不下的移动。

senses.title: According to
senses.definition: used in the phrase according to for a source of information
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 according to，表示信息来源
senses.example: According to the notice, the hall is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 根据告示，礼堂关闭。
senses.why: The information is measured against its source, which is the limit sense again.
senses.whyCN: 信息以其来源为界，又是界限义。

intro.en: The word is one of the oldest in the language, an Old English preposition of direction related to forms in other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: 这是语言中最古老的词之一，古英语中介词表示方向，与其它日耳曼语中的形式同源。

items.en: To meant toward, and also served to mark the person a thing was given to.
items.cn: 古英语 to 意为「朝向」，也用来标记接受某物的人。

items.en: Cognate forms in other Germanic languages carry the same direction sense.
items.cn: 其它日耳曼语中的同源形式带有同样的方向义。

items.en: The preposition was already used before a verb to express purpose.
items.cn: 这个介词已在动词前使用以表达目的。

items.en: Unstressed forms of the infinitive marker develop, giving the modern part of to.
items.cn: 不定式标记的弱读形式出现，成为现代 to 的一部分。

items.en: The unstressed pronunciation survives both as preposition and as infinitive marker.
items.cn: 弱读音在介词与不定式标记两种用法中都保留下来。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as to and fro and close to settle in the language.
items.cn: to and fro、close to 等固定短语在语言中定型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words often confused with this spelling, while the near-meaning group lists other prepositions of direction.
note.cn: 形近组收集容易与本词拼写混淆的词，近义组列出其它表示方向的介词。

entries.definitionCN: 也；太；只是读音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: the number after one, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 二；只是读音相同，词源不同

moving so as to be inside
moving so as to be on a surface

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the single direction image, the fixed phrases, and the confusing twins.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「朝向」这一单一意象、固定短语与易混词入手。

normal.en: To, too, and two sound alike and behave quite differently.
normal.cn: to、too、two 读音相同而用法完全不同。

normal.en: From A to B draws the whole line; to alone marks only its end.
normal.cn: from A to B 画出整条线，单是 to 只标出终点。

normal.en: The infinitive to appears where purpose or direction points at a verb.
normal.cn: 不定式 to 出现的地方，方向正指向一个动词。

normal.en: Ten to six counts up to the coming hour.
normal.cn: ten to six 是朝着下一个整点数。

normal.en: To and fro is a pair that never settles on a direction.
normal.cn: to and fro 是一对永远定不下来的方向。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn plainly from one dot to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一支清晰的箭，从一个点指向另一个点。

abstract.en: Think of a door pushed right up against its frame.
abstract.cn: 想一扇门被推到紧贴门框。

abstract.en: The little word is the shortest road between two words.
abstract.cn: 这个小词是两个词之间最短的一条路。

examples.en: We drove to the coast and back in one day.
examples.cn: 我们一天之内开车去了海边又回来。

examples.en: She gave the note to her brother.
examples.cn: 她把纸条给了弟弟。

examples.en: He turned to look at the clock.
examples.cn: 他转过身去看钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「土」——一路走到土里去，方向指得明明白白。

root: 古英语 to（朝向、到），日耳曼语族最古老的介词之一，与其它日耳曼语同源词同义；不定式标记由「朝向某个动作」的用法发展而来。

sensesIntro.en: Everything comes from pointing at a goal: a place, a limit, a receiver, an attitude, a coming hour, a verb to be done, or a purpose to be served.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都源于「指向目标」：地点、界限、受者、态度、下一个整点、要做的动词，或要达成的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pointing from where you are to a goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭从所在之处指向目标。

branches.en: Direction and the place it ends.
The receiver of a gift or an attitude.
Counting toward an hour and measuring against a source.
branches.cn: 朝整点数，以及依据来源衡量。

branches.en: Pointing at a verb or a purpose.
Reaching the frame, and moving back and forth.
branches.cn: 抵到门框，以及来回移动。

intro.cn: 这个功能词没有真正的词缀，但会组成复合词，并有规律的弱读形式。

definition_zh: 今天；今日；现今；当今；现在
definition_en: on or during the present day; also at the present period of history
core_image: 日历上被圈住的那一格，正是眼前这一天
scene: 窗外的树影还在原来的位置，只是叶子又落了一些。Today is warmer than yesterday, so the windows are open.
sceneCN: 这里 today 是「今天」（第 1 个义项：当前这一天）；句意为今天比昨天暖和，所以窗户都开着。画面有开着的窗、树影与日历。

derivatives.zh: 加所有格结尾，义为「今天的」
同构复合词，义为「今晚」
同族时间副词，义为「明天」

senses.title: The present day
senses.definition: the day on which someone is speaking or acting
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行动所处的这一天
senses.example: Today is warmer than yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 今天比昨天暖和。
senses.why: The word is a compound of to and day, literally on this day, first written as two words.
senses.whyCN: 本词由 to 与 day 复合而成，字面即「在这一天」，最初分写。

senses.title: On this day, as an adverb
senses.definition: during the present day, used to place an action in time
senses.definitionCN: 把动作定位在当日
senses.example: We are meeting the teacher today.
senses.exampleCN: 我们今天见老师。
senses.why: The same compound works as a time adverb without any preposition in front.
senses.whyCN: 同一复合词可作时间副词，前面不再需要介词。

senses.title: The present period
senses.definition: the present era or the current state of affairs
senses.definitionCN: 当前的年代或事务状况
senses.example: Today's students learn with devices in hand.
senses.exampleCN: 当今的学生手里拿着设备学习。
senses.why: A single day expands by metaphor to an age, since the present moment is felt as one long day.
senses.whyCN: 一天由比喻扩展为一个时代，因为当下被感知为漫长的一天。

senses.title: Nowadays
senses.definition: in the present time as compared with the past
senses.definitionCN: 与过去相比的现在
senses.example: Jobs today demand more flexibility than a century ago.
senses.exampleCN: 如今的工作比一个世纪前需要更多灵活性。
senses.why: Comparing past and present turns one day into a standpoint from which history is viewed.
senses.whyCN: 过去与现在的对照，把一天变成了观看历史的立场。

senses.title: Modern times
senses.definition: the modern period, especially in political or social writing
senses.definitionCN: 尤见于政治与社会写作中的现代
senses.example: Today differs from the past in how news travels.
senses.exampleCN: 今与昔的差别在于消息如何传播。
senses.why: Once today means the age, it can serve as a label for a whole social condition.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 today 指这个时代，就可作为整个社会状况的标签。

senses.title: The day in question
senses.definition: used of the day being discussed in a narrative
senses.definitionCN: 叙事中正在讨论的那一天
senses.example: They arrived on the morning of today's story.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在故事当天的早上到达。
senses.why: In a reported context, today is shifted to the day the speaker marked.
senses.whyCN: 在转述语境中，today 会移到说话者所指的那一天。

senses.title: Today's issue
senses.definition: used for a current item, as in today's agenda
senses.definitionCN: 用于当前事项，如 today's agenda
senses.example: Today's business is the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的议程是预算。
senses.why: A dated item belongs to today by definition, so the word labels what is current.
senses.whyCN: 当日之事自然属于今天，于是本词用来标示当下。

senses.title: An exclamation
senses.definition: used alone to mark that the day is the appointed time
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，表示所定的日子就是今天
senses.example: Today! The shop opens at last.
senses.exampleCN: 就在今天！店终于开了。
senses.why: Public announcements reuse the single day word as a dramatic marker.
senses.whyCN: 公告把这一天一词用作戏剧性的标记。

intro.en: It is a native English compound of to and day, written first as to day and joined in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土复合词，由 to 与 day 构成，起初写作 to day，十七世纪合为一词。

items.en: To meant at or on in certain time phrases, and daeg meant day.
items.cn: 古英语 to 在某些时间短语中意为「在」，daeg 意为「一天」。

items.en: The phrase to day appears written as two words meaning on this day.
items.cn: to day 一语出现，分写，意为「在这一天」。

items.en: The compound begins to be treated as a single word.
items.cn: 这个复合词开始被当作一个词处理。

items.en: The spelling today with one word becomes standard.
items.cn: 合写形式 today 成为标准。

items.en: The word extends from the day to the present age.
items.cn: 本词从这一天扩展到当今时代。

items.en: Tonight and tomorrow follow the same compound pattern.
items.cn: tonight 与 tomorrow 遵循同样的复合方式。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers near compounds of time, and the near-meaning group lists other markers of the present.
note.cn: 形近组收集相近的时间复合词，近义组列出其它表示当下的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the two halves, the spelling history, and the pattern with its neighbours.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从两半构词、拼写史以及与邻居的同一模式入手。

normal.en: Today is to plus day, meaning on this day.
normal.cn: today 是 to 加 day，意为在这一天。

normal.en: Tonight and tomorrow are built the same way, so learn all three together.
normal.cn: tonight、tomorrow 同法构成，三个一起记。

normal.en: Today's world uses today as an age, not just a day.
normal.cn: today's world 里的 today 指一个时代，而不只是一天。

normal.en: The apostrophe in today's is possessives of time, not a contraction.
normal.cn: today's 里的撇号是时间所有格，不是缩略。

normal.en: Comparing with yesterday turns today into a standpoint.
normal.cn: 与 yesterday 对比，today 就成了一个立场。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar square circled once in red.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一格用红笔圈了一次。

abstract.en: Think of a window open to the morning air.
abstract.cn: 想一扇向晨风敞开的窗。

abstract.en: Every age calls itself today while it lasts.
abstract.cn: 每个时代在它存在时都自称今天。

examples.en: Today is the first day of the new term.
examples.cn: 今天是新学期的第一天。

examples.en: She bought today's paper on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家路上她买了今天的报纸。

examples.en: Today, most letters are read on a screen.
examples.cn: 如今大多数信件都在屏幕上读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特得」——特别得到了一天，就是今天。

root: 由古英语介词 to（在此意义上为「在」）与 daeg（日）复合而成，中古英语分写 to day，十七世纪合写为 today，后引申为「现今」。

sensesIntro.en: One circled square on the calendar serves as a day, a speaking moment, an age, and a standpoint from which history is compared.
sensesIntro.cn: 日历上一格被圈住的方框，既是某一天，也是说话之时、一个时代，乃至比较历史的立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one calendar square we are standing inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：我们正站在其中的那一格日历。

branches.en: The day itself, as noun and adverb.
branches.cn: 这一天本身，作名词与副词。

branches.en: The age that calls itself now.
The standpoint for comparing past and present.
branches.cn: 比较过去与现在的立场。

branches.en: The current item on hand.
The dramatic alone use.
branches.cn: 单独使用的戏剧性用法。

intro.en: The word is a closed compound of two native elements, and its endings are possessives rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个本土成分紧缩而成，其尾加成分是所有格而非后缀。

latinIntro.en: Nothing Latin lies behind today; the Latin list offers borrowed time words for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: today 背后没有拉丁语；拉丁表提供时间类借词作对照。

This half names the unit.
Today's paper is the paper of this day.
items.exampleCN: today's paper 是今天的报纸。

items.example: Todays is used only of several present-day periods.
Todayness is a coined word for the quality of the present.
items.exampleCN: today-ness 是生造词，指当下性。

items.example: Daytime pairs similarly.
Daylight follows the same pattern.
Daybreak names the morning.

definition_zh: 一起；共同；合起来；连续地；（get together）聚会
definition_en: with another person or thing, in one place or as one group; also in an unbroken sequence
core_image: 两双手伸到一处，掌与掌合拢成一点
scene: 晚饭前，桌上的碗筷被一只只摆好，孩子在旁边帮忙。The family put the table together before dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 together 是「一起、共同」（第 1 个义项：与他人或他物相聚一处）；句意为一家人在晚饭前一起把桌子拼好。画面有桌面、碗筷与帮忙的孩子。

pos.zh: 副词：一起；共同；合起来；连续地

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「亲密；团结」
加前缀 al- 变体构成，义为「完全；总共」
复合词，义为「聚会」

senses.title: With one another
senses.definition: with another person or group, in each other's company
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或群体在一处、同在一行
senses.example: They worked together all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个下午一起工作。
senses.why: Old English togædere was a phrase meaning to and in a gathering, that is, into one place.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 togædere 意为「聚到一处」，即合成一个地方。

senses.title: In one place or whole
senses.definition: so as to form one group, set, or whole
senses.definitionCN: 聚成一群、一套或一个整体
senses.example: She tied the branches together.
senses.exampleCN: 她把树枝捆在一起。
senses.why: The gathering sense becomes the act of joining parts into a unit.
senses.whyCN: 「聚拢」义延伸为把部分合成整体。

senses.title: In cooperation
senses.definition: in shared effort toward a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标协作
senses.example: The whole street pulled together during the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水期间整条街的人齐心协力。
senses.why: People who are physically gathered can act as one, and the word marks that shared effort.
senses.whyCN: 身体聚在一处的人可以一起行动，本词便标示这种共同用力。

senses.title: In continuous succession
senses.definition: used with plural time words for an unbroken run
senses.definitionCN: 与表示时段的复数连用，指不间断的一段
senses.example: It rained for three days together.
senses.exampleCN: 雨连续下了三天。
senses.why: Things placed one after another without a gap are together in a row as well as in space.
senses.whyCN: 彼此紧挨、无缝排列的东西，在时间上也是连着的一串。

senses.title: To assemble
senses.definition: used with put to make or assemble something from parts
senses.definitionCN: 与 put 连用，指由零件组成
senses.example: He put the shelf together in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他一小时就把架子组装好了。
senses.why: Assembling is the literal gathering of parts into one object.
senses.whyCN: 组装就是把零件真正聚成一个物件。

senses.title: In company with
senses.definition: used in together with to add something to what is already stated
senses.definitionCN: 用于 together with，把某物加上去
senses.example: The rent, together with heating, comes to a thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 房租加取暖费一共一千。
senses.why: Adding to a group is gathering the new item into the existing set.
senses.whyCN: 加入群体就是把新项聚进已有的集合。

senses.title: In harmony
senses.definition: in agreement or well matched
senses.definitionCN: 和谐、相配、一致
senses.example: The colours in the room go together well.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的颜色很协调。
senses.why: Two things that fit join without a seam, which is gathering without friction.
senses.whyCN: 相配的两物无缝相接，正是无摩擦的聚合。

senses.title: The act of meeting
senses.definition: used in get-together for a social meeting
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get-together，指社交聚会
senses.example: A small get-together was held after the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 典礼后举行了一场小型聚会。
senses.why: The adverb becomes a noun in the compound, naming the meeting it describes.
senses.whyCN: 副词在复合词中变作名词，命名其所描述的会面。

intro.en: Old English had togædere, built from to and a form of gathering, so the original picture is movement into one place.
intro.cn: 古英语已有 togædere，由 to 与表示聚集的成分构成，原图景是「聚到一处」。

items.en: Togædere meant into one place, in a body.
items.cn: togædere 意为聚到一处、在一体之中。

items.en: The second element is related to gathering, giving the whole word a pull inward.
items.cn: 第二成分与「聚集」相关，使整词带有向内收拢的意思。

items.en: The form settles toward together, dropping the older ending.
items.cn: 形式趋于 together，古旧词尾脱落。

items.en: The word extends from place to shared action.
items.cn: 本词从地点扩展到共同行动。

items.en: The phrase for days together develops for continuous periods.
items.cn: for days together 这样的短语发展出「连续时段」义。

items.en: Togetherness appears as a noun for the feeling of closeness.
items.cn: togetherness 作为名词出现，指亲密之感。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers its derived and near forms, and the near-meaning group lists other words for joint action.
note.cn: 形近组收集派生与相近形式，近义组列出表示共同行动的其他词。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the gathering picture, the fixed phrases, and the derived nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「聚到一处」的图景、固定短语与派生名词入手。

normal.en: Together is to plus gather, the two halves of pulling things in.
normal.cn: together 是 to 加 gather，两半合起来就是向内收拢。

normal.en: Get together, pull together, put together all add a verb of motion.
normal.cn: get together、pull together、put together 都叠加了动作动词。

normal.en: Together with adds an item; altogether means completely.
normal.cn: together with 是加上一项，altogether 是完全、总共。

normal.en: For days together marks an unbroken run of time.
normal.cn: for days together 标记连续不断的一段时间。

normal.en: Togetherness turns the adverb into a quality of a group.
normal.cn: togetherness 把副词变成群体的品性。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting at a single point.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在一点上合拢。

abstract.en: Think of two branches bound with one cord.
abstract.cn: 想两根树枝被一根绳捆在一起。

abstract.en: A whole street pulling a rope is the word in action.

definition_zh: 明天；明日；未来；将来
definition_en: the day after today, or the near future that has not come yet
core_image: 窗外的天色还没亮，桌上放着一张写着明日的车票
scene: 深夜的教室里，最后一盏灯也要熄了，值日生把黑板擦干净才走。The exam is tomorrow morning, so everyone went to bed early.
sceneCN: 这里 tomorrow 是「明天」这一天（第 1 个义项：今天的下一天）；句意为考试就在明天上午，于是大家都早早上床。画面里有熄灯的教室、擦净的黑板与走廊。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「一个又一个明天」

senses.title: The day after today
senses.definition: the day that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: We will finish the report tomorrow, before the office opens.
senses.exampleCN: 我们明天在办公室开门前把报告写完。
senses.why: The Old English form joins the word for morrow with the preposition to, so the word literally points at the next day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式把表示「次日」的词与介词 to 连在一起，字面上就是「指向下一天」。

senses.title: The near future
senses.definition: the time that is still to come, especially the near future
senses.definitionCN: 尚未到来的时间，尤指不久之后
senses.example: The engineers spoke of the city of tomorrow as if they could already walk in it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们谈起未来的城市，仿佛已经能在其中行走。
senses.why: One step beyond the next morning, the word becomes a name for any time not yet reached.
senses.whyCN: 再往前一步，这个词就成了任何尚未抵达之时间的名字。

senses.title: Morning as a time of day
senses.definition: in older usage, the morning hours of any day
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，任何一天的早晨时段
senses.example: Good morrow to you, the old greeting said, wishing a fine morning.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的问候语会说 good morrow，祝愿对方有个美好的早晨。
senses.why: The morrow of the word is the same morrow that meant morning, and that older sense survives in greetings.
senses.whyCN: 词中的 morrow 就是表示「早晨」的那个 morrow，这个古义在问候语里留了下来。

senses.title: A promise about the future
senses.definition: a pledge that something will be done on the next day or later
senses.definitionCN: 保证在某天或之后去做某事的承诺
senses.example: He kept saying tomorrow, and the fence was never painted.
senses.exampleCN: 他总说明天，篱笆却始终没有刷。
senses.why: Because the next day is always available in speech, tomorrow becomes the natural home of postponed promises.
senses.whyCN: 因为口语里永远还有下一个明天，tomorrow 就自然成了拖延承诺的落脚处。

senses.title: The next issue or edition
senses.definition: used in publishing for the edition that comes out on the next day
senses.definitionCN: 出版业中指第二天出的那一期
senses.example: The editor held the story for tomorrow's paper and let the evening edition go without it.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把这条新闻留到明天的报纸，晚报就先不带它。
senses.why: Editors work a day ahead, so the next day's date in a masthead is simply the word for the coming edition.
senses.whyCN: 编辑总是提前一天工作，于是报头上第二天的日期就顺理成章成了「下一期」的代称。

senses.title: A future opportunity
senses.definition: a chance that will appear later rather than now
senses.definitionCN: 以后而不是现在才出现的机会
senses.example: There is always tomorrow, said the coach, meaning the next match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练说总还有明天，意思是还有下一场比赛。
senses.why: When a loss must be comforted, the next day becomes the name of hope itself.
senses.whyCN: 需要安慰一场失利时，下一天就成了希望这个名字。

senses.title: The future as a shared project
senses.definition: the future considered as something a group works towards together
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个群体共同为之努力的未来
senses.example: The village meeting was really about tomorrow, not about the drains.
senses.exampleCN: 村会的真正议题是未来，而不是下水道。
senses.why: The word can stand for the whole horizon a community plans for, once it stops meaning one date.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不再指某个日期，这个词就能代表一个共同体规划的整片地平线。

senses.title: Time treated as an ordinary commodity
senses.definition: the next day as a plain unit of scheduling, without emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 作为普通日程单位的下一天，不带强调
senses.example: Tomorrow suits me better than Friday, if that is all right.
senses.exampleCN: 如果方便的话，明天比周五更适合我。
senses.why: Here the word carries no weight beyond the calendar, which is how it appears in most everyday planning.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词除了日历之外不携带任何分量，多数日常安排里它就是这样出现的。

senses.title: The adverb of the next day
senses.definition: as an adverb, on the day following today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: She will drive north tomorrow and be back by Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 她明天开车北上，周日之前回来。
senses.why: The noun and the adverb share one shape, so the word sits in a sentence without any preposition at all.
senses.whyCN: 名词与副词同形，因此这个词可以不带任何介词直接进入句子。

intro.en: Tomorrow is a native English compound: the preposition to joined to morrow, an old word for the next day or the morning.
intro.cn: tomorrow 是英语本土复合词：介词 to 加上 morrow（古义为次日、早晨）。

items.en: The word morgen means morning, and morrow in the phrase on the morrow refers to the following day.
items.cn: 古英语 morgen 意为早晨，短语 on the morrow 里的 morrow 指紧接着的那一天。

items.en: To morgen, written as two words, points forward to the next morning and is the direct ancestor of the modern form.
items.cn: 写作两个词的 to morgen 表示「到明天早晨」，是现代形式的直接祖先。

items.en: The two elements merge into a single word to morwe, later tomorrow, while morrow keeps the older sense separately.
items.cn: 两个成分合并为一词 to morwe，后来成为 tomorrow，而 morrow 另行保留古义。

items.en: The word settles into its present spelling in the sixteenth century and takes over the adverbial use from the phrase on the morrow.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪定下现在的拼写，并接替短语 on the morrow 的副词用法。

items.en: From the eighteenth century tomorrow extends beyond the next day to mean the indefinite future.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，tomorrow 由「次日」扩展到指不确定的未来。

items.en: In modern speech it also stands alone as a promise or a postponement, as in tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.
items.cn: 现代口语里它也单独用作承诺或拖延的说法，正如「明天，明天，再一个明天」那一句。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other words of the same to- family in time words, while the near-meaning group gathers terms for the days and the future.
note.cn: 形近组收集时间词里由 to- 构成的同族词，近义组则汇集表示日期与未来的词。

normal.en: Morrow is the second half, and it survives alone in literary English.

normal.en: There is no preposition: we say I will go tomorrow, not on tomorrow.
normal.cn: 这里不用介词：说 I will go tomorrow，而不是 on tomorrow。

definition_zh: 今晚；今夜；今晚的（活动）
definition_en: the night or evening of the present day, or during that night
core_image: 街上灯一盏盏亮起来，剧场门口的灯箱写着今晚的场次
scene: 厨房里碗刚洗完，桌上还留着两杯热茶，窗外的天已经黑透了。The concert is tonight, so we should leave before seven.
sceneCN: 这里 tonight 指「今晚这一夜」（第 1 个义项：今天晚上的时间）；句意为音乐会就在今晚，我们七点前该出发。画面里有夜色、洗好的碗与等着出门的动作。

同一构词模式的同族词，义为「明天」

senses.title: The night of today
senses.definition: the night or evening that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 今天之后的那个夜晚或傍晚
senses.example: We are staying in tonight because of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 因为暴风雨，我们今晚待在家里。
senses.why: The word is a preposition fused to night, so it points at the dark part of the current day.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是介词与 night 的融合，指向当天的黑暗时段。

senses.title: During the coming night
senses.definition: as an adverb, during the night that follows today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一夜里
senses.example: The temperature will fall below zero tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚气温会降到零度以下。
senses.why: As an adverb the word needs no preposition, which is why we say tonight rather than in tonight.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时这个词不带介词，所以只说 tonight 而不说 in tonight。

senses.title: A scheduled event for today
senses.definition: the arrangement, programme, or performance set for the present evening
senses.definitionCN: 安排在今晚的活动、节目或演出
senses.example: Tonight's match has been moved to the smaller ground.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚的比赛已经改到较小的球场。
senses.why: With the possessive the word works as a noun, and that shift lets it label an event rather than a time.
senses.whyCN: 加所有格后它充当名词，这一转变使它能够标示一场活动而非一段时间。

senses.title: The present evening as a unit of plans
senses.definition: the present evening considered as the block of time available for plans
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚看作可用来安排事情的一段时间
senses.example: I have the whole of tonight to finish the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 我有一整晚的时间读完这一章。
senses.why: Once it names a block of hours, the word can take quantity phrases like the whole of.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它指一段时辰，就能接 the whole of 这样的数量短语。

senses.title: The word in broadcasts
senses.definition: used in news and broadcasts to mark the report of the present day
senses.definitionCN: 新闻与广播中用来标明当天的报道
senses.example: Tonight we report on the election results from three regions.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚我们报道三个地区的选举结果。
senses.why: A broadcast must fix the day on which the listener hears it, so the word becomes a standard opening marker.
senses.whyCN: 广播必须钉住听众听到它的那一天，于是这个词成了标准的开场标记。

senses.title: An evening out
senses.definition: the evening's entertainment, especially when it is planned
senses.definitionCN: 今晚的娱乐活动，尤指事先安排好的
senses.example: Tonight is our anniversary dinner, so the whole family is coming.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚是我们的周年晚餐，全家人都来。
senses.why: In the phrase tonight is our dinner, the word stands in for the whole arrangement of the evening.
senses.whyCN: 在「今晚是我们的晚餐」这句话里，这个词代表整个晚上的安排。

senses.title: The coming night as a deadline
senses.definition: the present evening as the moment by which something must be done
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚当作某事必须完成的时刻
senses.example: The report has to be in tonight, or the printer will miss the morning edition.
senses.exampleCN: 报告今晚必须交，否则印刷厂会赶不上早报。
senses.why: Because the evening ends at midnight, the word can act as a deadline that is still ahead.
senses.whyCN: 因为夜晚到午夜就结束，这个词可以充当一个尚未到达的截止时刻。

senses.title: The word as a farewell
senses.definition: used in a farewell to mean that the speaker expects to meet again the same evening
senses.definitionCN: 道别时说，表示今晚还会再见
senses.example: See you tonight, she said, and closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她说了句今晚见，就把门关上了。
senses.why: A farewell can safely point at tonight because the same evening has still to happen.
senses.whyCN: 道别时可以放心指向今晚，因为这一晚还没发生。

intro.en: Tonight is a native compound of the preposition to and the noun night, built on the same model as today and tomorrow.
intro.cn: tonight 是介词 to 与名词 night 构成的本土复合词，其模式与 today、tomorrow 相同。

items.en: The phrase to niht, written as two words, means in or during this night.
items.cn: 古英语短语 to niht 写作两个词，意为今夜、在这夜里。

items.en: The two words begin to be written as one, toniht, and the sense narrows to the present evening.
items.cn: 两个词开始连写为 toniht，含义收窄为今晚。

items.en: The modern spelling tonight is fixed in the eighteenth century, at the same time as today takes its present form.
items.cn: 现代拼写 tonight 于十八世纪定型，与 today 定型的时间相同。

items.en: The noun use appears as soon as the compound is felt to be one word, as in the preparations for tonight.
items.cn: 一旦这个复合词被感觉成一个词，名词用法就出现了，如「为今晚做准备」。

items.en: Broadcasting gives the word a fixed function as a time marker at the start of reports.
items.cn: 广播让这个词固定承担在报道开头标示时间的职能。

items.en: In speech it also serves as a farewell, since the same evening is still to come.
items.cn: 口语里它还是道别语，因为那一晚还没过去。

examples.en: There is a film on television tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚电视上有一部电影。

examples.en: Tonight's dinner will be simple because we are late.
examples.cn: 因为回来晚，今晚的晚饭就简单点。

examples.en: Will you be free tonight to look at the plans?
examples.cn: 今晚你有空看一下这些图纸吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特耐特」——今晚的夜特别耐熬，特能熬到很晚。

root: 古英语短语 to niht（在今夜）→ 中古英语 toniht → 现代 tonight。由介词 to 与 night 合成；同族词 today、tomorrow。

sensesIntro.en: The entry moves from the night that follows today, through its adverbial use, scheduled events, and broadcast use, to the small social phrases that carry it in daily speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从今天之后的那一夜写起，经副词用法、安排好的活动与广播用语，最后落到日常生活里承载它的那些小短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointed at the darkness of the coming night.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指指向即将降临的那片夜色。

branches.en: The night itself and the adverbial use.
An event arranged for the evening.
The evening as usable time or as a deadline.
branches.cn: 今晚作为可用时间或期限。

branches.en: The fixed use in news and broadcasts.
branches.cn: 新闻与广播中的固定用法。

branches.en: The word as a goodbye.

intro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; English pieces are simply the preposition and the noun, plus the plural and possessive endings.
intro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语祖先；其英语成分只是介词与名词，外加复数与所有格词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source exists, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: The first element points at the coming night.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分指向即将到来的夜。

items.example: Night is the second element.
The Old English form is written niht.

items.meaning: a silent letter kept in some words
items.meaningCN: 某些词中保留的不发音字母
items.example: Night keeps the gh that is no longer spoken.
items.exampleCN: night 保留了已不发音的 gh。

items.meaning: used in a few fixed phrases
items.example: Tonight is not used in the plural.
Tonight's show uses the possessive.

items.meaning: the light part of a day
items.example: Day forms the second half of today.
items.exampleCN: day 构成 today 的后半部分。

items.example: Morrow forms tomorrow with the same to-.
items.exampleCN: morrow 与同样的 to- 构成 tomorrow。

items.example: Midnight uses the same night with a modifier.
items.exampleCN: midnight 用同一个 night 加修饰成分。

definition_zh: 也；还；太；过于
definition_en: also, or more than is wanted or needed, or to a higher degree than is acceptable
core_image: 一只杯子里倒水，水面已经高过杯沿，再多一滴就要溢出来
scene: 试衣服的人站在镜子前拉了拉肩线，回头看了一眼同伴。The jacket is nice, but it is too tight across the shoulders.
sceneCN: 这里 too 表示「过于」（第 2 个义项：超过可接受程度）；句意为这件外套不错，但肩部太紧了。画面里有试衣镜、拉肩线的动作与同伴的眼神。

pos.zh: 副词：非常；很（口语中作加强）

derivatives.zh: 只差一个字母的介词，读音相近，作用完全不同
只差一个字母的数词，读音相同，含义不同
最接近「也」这一义项的正式说法
最接近「过于」这一义项的书面说法

senses.title: Also, in addition
senses.definition: as well, in addition to what has been mentioned, usually at the end of a clause
senses.definitionCN: 此外、同样地，通常位于句末
senses.example: She plays the violin, and she sings too.
senses.exampleCN: 她拉小提琴，也唱歌。
senses.why: The word is a stressed form of to, and the sense of addition grew out of the idea of going along with something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 to 的重读形式，「也」的含义由「随之而去」的意思长出来。

senses.title: More than is wanted
senses.definition: to a greater degree than is suitable, pleasant, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 达到超出适宜、愉快或可接受的程度
senses.example: The soup is too salty to drink.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤太咸，喝不下去。
senses.why: Beyond is the second sense the Old English adverb carried, and it names the point where a limit has been passed.
senses.whyCN: 「超出」是古英语副词本来就有的第二个含义，它标示限度被越过的位置。

senses.title: Very, as an intensifier
senses.definition: in informal speech, a mild intensifier meaning very
senses.definitionCN: 口语中轻微的加强语，意为很
senses.example: I am not too sure about that plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那个计划不太有把握。
senses.why: Said with a falling voice, the word softens rather than sharpens, and that mild use is purely a habit of speech.
senses.whyCN: 压低语调说出时，它起缓和作用而非加强，这种轻微用法纯属口语习惯。

senses.title: A regretful excess
senses.definition: used to point at an excess that has unfortunate results
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出造成不幸结果的过头之处
senses.example: It was too late to change the ticket when we reached the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到车站时，改签已经太晚了。
senses.why: Regret is what an excess leaves behind, so the word often appears in complaints about what is past changing.
senses.whyCN: 惋惜是「过头」留下的余味，所以这个词常出现在抱怨已无法改变之事的句子里。

senses.title: A polite refusal
senses.definition: used with a negative to soften a refusal or an apology
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，使拒绝或道歉显得委婉
senses.example: It is not too far, if we take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 如果坐公交，也不算太远。
senses.why: A negative before the word cancels the excess, which is how English makes a refusal sound gentler.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词前加否定就取消了「过头」，英语正是用这种方式让拒绝听起来温和。

senses.title: A comparison of degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to show that a limit has been passed
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明某项限度已被越过
senses.example: The room is too small for six chairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这房间太小，放不下六把椅子。
senses.why: The word always looks for an adjective or adverb to lean on, and that pairing is what makes a comparison of degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个词总要依附一个形容词或副词，这种搭配才构成程度上的比较。

senses.title: An emphatic agreement
senses.definition: in replies, an emphatic agreement with a negative or positive statement
senses.definitionCN: 在回应中表示强烈的赞同
senses.example: You were right. You were, too.
senses.exampleCN: 你说得对，确实对。
senses.why: In a reply the word can be added at the end to strengthen what the other person just said.
senses.whyCN: 在回应中把它加在句末，就能加强对方刚说过的话。

senses.title: A fixed adverbial phrase
senses.definition: used in set phrases to comment on frequency or degree
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语中评论频率或程度
senses.example: All too often the letter arrives after the meeting has ended.
senses.exampleCN: 信件往往在会议结束后才到。
senses.why: Fossil phrases keep old patterns alive, and all too often is a set comment on how frequently an excess happens.
senses.whyCN: 凝固短语让旧结构存活，all too often 就是一句固定的评论，说明某种过分之事发生得多频繁。

intro.en: Too is a stressed doublet of to, both descending from Old English to, and the sense of addition grew alongside the prepositional sense.
intro.cn: too 是 to 的重读同源形式，二者都来自古英语 to，「也」的含义与介词义并存发展。

items.en: To serves as preposition and adverb, covering towards, in addition, and beyond.
items.cn: 古英语 to 兼作介词与副词，涵盖「朝向」「此外」与「超出」等义。

items.en: The unstressed form to continues as the preposition, and the stressed form develops separately.
items.cn: 非重读形式 to 继续作介词，重读形式则单独发展。

items.en: The stressed form is written as to, too, or two, and the spelling settles as too in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 重读形式曾写作 to、too 或 two，拼写于十六世纪定为 too。

items.en: The sense of also becomes the common one, working in the same way as the German auch.
items.cn: 「也」成为最常见的义项，其功能与德语 auch 相似。

items.en: The excess sense is fixed in the phrases too much and too many, which become the standard counters of excess.
items.cn: 「过度」义固定在 too much 与 too many 两个短语里，成为表示过分的标准说法。

items.en: The informal intensifier use, as in not too bad, spreads in speech from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 口语中「不太差」这类轻度加强用法自十八世纪起扩散。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ by one letter and cause spelling errors, while the near-meaning group gathers the adverbs of addition and degree.
note.cn: 形近组收集只差一个字母、容易拼错的词，近义组则汇集表示「也」与程度的副词。

entries.definition: a preposition of direction, or the infinitive marker
the number 2
an instrument used to do work
throughout a period
entries.definitionCN: 在……期间，只是词形近似，词源不同

entries.definition: in addition, in more formal writing
in addition, at the end of a clause
to a harmful or wasteful degree
to the degree needed and no more

normalIntro.en: These memories separate the three jobs of the word and use the fixed phrases where each one lives.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条把这个词的三个职能分开，并利用各自所在的固定短语。

normal.en: Too is a stressed to: one o more and one stress more, and the sense of addition turns into excess.
normal.cn: too 是重读的 to：多一个 o、多一分重音，「附加」就变成「过头」。

normal.en: Too comes at the end of a clause for also, but before an adjective for excess.
normal.cn: 表示「也」时位于句末，表示「过于」时位于形容词之前。

normal.en: Too much goes with uncountable nouns and too many with plural ones.
normal.cn: too much 接不可数名词，too many 接复数名词。

normal.en: Too ... to ... is the pattern of impossibility: too tired to walk.
normal.cn: too...to... 表示无法做到：太累而走不动。

normal.en: Me too is short for I think so too, and it drops the whole verb.
normal.cn: me too 是 I think so too 的省略，动词整个省掉了。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase that closes only when someone sits on it, and that is too full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只得坐上去才关得上的箱子，那就是「太满」。

abstract.en: Think of one more guest arriving at a table that already has every chair taken.
abstract.cn: 想一张椅子已坐满的桌子又来了一位客人。

abstract.en: Too is the word for the moment a good thing crosses the line into a problem.
abstract.cn: too 就是好事越过界线变成问题那一刻的词。

examples.en: The tea is too hot to drink now.
examples.cn: 茶太烫，现在喝不了。

examples.en: He works in the city and teaches at weekends too.
examples.cn: 他在城里工作，周末也教书。

examples.en: There were too many people in the small hall.
examples.cn: 小礼堂里人太多了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐」——太撑了就想吐，足见 too 的「过分」。

root: 古英语 to（介词兼副词）的重读形式，与非重读的 to 同源；十六世纪定型为 too。与 to、two 只差一个字母，读音相同而易混。

sensesIntro.en: The word has three jobs: adding to what was said, pushing past a limit, and, in speech, lightly intensifying. The entry moves through each job and through the fixed phrases built on them.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词有三种职能：补充前面所说的、越过限度、以及口语中的轻度加强。条目沿着这三种职能与建在其上的固定短语展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup filled past the point where it can hold more.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被倒到多过其容量的杯子。

branches.en: Adding to a statement and agreeing with it.
Passing a limit and pointing at the result.
branches.cn: 越过限度并指出其后果。

branches.en: Soft intensifiers in informal speech.
Fixed phrases of frequency and degree.
branches.cn: 频率与程度的固定短语。

branches.en: The end position that marks also.

intro.en: The word is a single stressed adverb with no affixes of its own; its interest lies in the fixed phrases it forms.
intro.cn: 本词是单个重读副词，本身不带词缀，其要点在于所构成的固定短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: The word is one unstressed root.
items.exampleCN: 本词是一个不带词缀的词根。

items.example: To is spelled with one o.
Two has a w that too lacks.
items.exampleCN: two 比 too 多一个 w。

items.meaning: a large amount of an uncountable thing
items.example: Too much marks excess of amount.
items.exampleCN: too much 表示数量过分。

items.meaning: a large number of countable things
items.example: Too many marks excess of number.
items.exampleCN: too many 表示数目过多。

items.example: Excessively is the formal adverb for the same idea.
items.exampleCN: excessively 是同一意思的书面副词。

items.example: Too late is a fixed phrase.
All too often is a fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: all too often 是固定短语。

items.meaning: the second o marks stress and length
items.meaningCN: 多出的 o 表示重读与长音
items.example: The spelling too keeps the long vowel visible.
items.exampleCN: 拼写 too 用双 o 显出长元音。

definition_zh: 工具；器具；手段；（软件）工具；用工具加工
definition_en: an object, usually held in the hand, that is made to help do work, or any means used to achieve something
core_image: 一只木柄的手锤靠在墙边，锤头上的磨痕说明它被用得很多
scene: 木工台面上散着凿子、卷尺和几块未刨的木料，墙上的木板插满了带柄的工具。He laid each tool back in its place before turning off the light.
sceneCN: 这里 tool 是「工具」这一类物件（第 1 个义项：手持以帮助工作的器物）；句意为他在关灯前把每件工具都放回原位。画面里有木工台、凿子、卷尺与墙上挂满工具的木架。

pos.zh: 动词：用工具加工；给……装上工具

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「工具（复数）」
由 tool 与 kit 合成，义为「工具套装；方法组合」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「模具工装；加工」
由 tool 与 box 合成，义为「工具箱」

senses.title: An object made to help with work
senses.definition: a device, usually held in the hand, that is made to do a job more easily
senses.definitionCN: 通常手持的器具，制成以后使工作更容易完成
senses.example: A good spade is the only tool you need for this bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这块花圃只需要一把好铲子这件工具。
senses.why: The word is one of the oldest in English, and the earliest senses cover any instrument of labour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语最古老的词之一，最早的义项涵盖任何劳作器械。

senses.title: A means of achieving something
senses.definition: anything used by a person or group to reach an end
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体用来达到目的的任何东西
senses.example: Language is the chief tool of the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是历史学家的主要工具。
senses.why: Anything that extends what a person can do counts as an instrument, so the word moves easily from metal to method.
senses.whyCN: 任何能扩展人所能做之事的东西都算器械，所以这个词很自然地从金属移到方法。

senses.title: A person used by another
senses.definition: someone who is used by others to do their work or to carry out their plans
senses.definitionCN: 被他人利用来做事或实现其计划的人
senses.example: He was a tool of the men who really ran the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他不过是真正操控委员会那些人手里的工具。
senses.why: A person who merely carries out another's purpose is treated like an implement, and the metaphor is deliberately unkind.
senses.whyCN: 只是实现他人目的的人被当成器物，这个比喻是刻意刻薄的。

senses.title: A set of software functions
senses.definition: a program or function that helps carry out a specific task
senses.definitionCN: 帮助完成某项特定任务的程序或功能
senses.example: The new tool lets you compare two versions of the same document.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新工具可以比较同一文档的两个版本。
senses.why: Software repeats the oldest pattern in the language: a thing made to make work easier, this time without metal.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复了语言里最古老的一套用法：为使工作更易而造出的东西，只是这回没有金属。

senses.title: The cutting part of a machine
senses.definition: the cutting or shaping part of a machine, such as a drill bit
senses.definitionCN: 机床中切削或成形的部件，如钻头
senses.example: Change the tool before the edge dulls completely.
senses.exampleCN: 在刃口完全变钝之前换掉刀具。
senses.why: A machine works by cutting with a tool, so the cutting part inherits the name of the hand tool it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 机器靠刀具切削工作，于是这个切削部件继承了他所取代的手持工具之名。

senses.title: To shape with tools
senses.definition: to cut, shape, or decorate something with a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用工具切割、成形或装饰某物
senses.example: The leather was tooled with a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这块皮革用小花纹压出了图案。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: to work a material with a tool until a pattern appears.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：用工具加工材料，直到出现花纹。

senses.title: To equip for work
senses.definition: to provide a workshop or factory with the tools it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为作坊或工厂提供所需的工具
senses.example: The plant was tooled up for a new model in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在春季为一种新车型配齐了工装。
senses.why: Equipping a plant is giving it tools at industrial scale, and the same verb covers the workshop and the shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 给工厂装备工具就是工业规模上的「给工具」，同一个动词兼指车间与流水线。

senses.title: To drive a vehicle
senses.definition: in informal speech, to drive a vehicle, especially steadily along
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指开车，尤指平稳前行
senses.example: We tooled along the river road all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午沿着河边公路开车闲逛。
senses.why: The slang sense treats a car as the tool of the journey and the driving as working it along.
senses.whyCN: 俚语义把汽车当作旅程的工具，开车就是把这件工具一路使过去。

senses.title: A plain phrase in computing
senses.definition: a small program run from a command line to perform one task quickly
senses.definitionCN: 在命令行运行以快速完成单项任务的小程序
senses.example: A single command-line tool replaced three old scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 一个命令行工具就取代了三个旧脚本。
senses.why: Computing names its small single-purpose programs tools because each one does one job well in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把单项用途的小程序称作工具，因为每一件就在手中把一件事做好。

intro.en: Tool is an inherited Germanic word, recorded in Old English as tol, and its prehistory beyond the Germanic languages is uncertain.
intro.cn: tool 是继承的日耳曼语词，古英语记作 tol，其在日耳曼语系之外的更早来源尚不确定。

items.en: Tol is used of any instrument or implement, including weapons and writing implements.
items.cn: 古英语 tol 用于任何器械或工具，包括武器与书写用具。

items.en: The stem tolam is shared with Old Norse tol and related forms meaning an implement.
items.cn: 词干 tolam 与古诺斯语 tol 以及表示工具的若干同源形式共有。

items.en: Middle English tool spreads to cover hand tools of every trade and keeps the general sense of a means.
items.cn: 中古英语 tool 扩展到各种手艺的手持工具，并保留「手段」的一般含义。

items.en: The verb appears in the nineteenth century, first for shaping by hand and later for fitting a factory with machines.
items.cn: 动词用法出现于十九世纪，先指手工成形，后指为工厂配备机器。

items.en: The slang sense of a person used by others is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 「被人利用的人」这一俚语义自十六世纪有记录。

items.en: Computing borrows the word for programs, and software tools become one of the commonest uses today.
items.cn: 计算机领域借用这个词指程序，软件工具成了今天最常见的用法之一。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and near spellings, while the near-meaning group gathers words for instruments and for means.
note.cn: 形近组收集复合词与近似拼写，近义组则汇集表示器具与手段的词。

entries.definition: a set of tools, or a set of methods
a box for keeping tools
the tools and equipment needed for manufacture
also, or excessively
entries.definitionCN: 也；太，只是拼写近似，词源不同

entries.definition: a device used for careful work, often medical or musical
a simple tool used out of doors or in a trade
a machine made for a particular purpose
a tool used in a kitchen or household

normalIntro.en: These memories use the Old English word, the compounds with box and kit, and the way the word slides from objects to means to software.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用古英语原词、与 box 和 kit 构成的复合词，以及这个词由实物滑向手段再到软件的过程。

normal.en: Old English tol is short and plain, and it still names anything that helps you work.
normal.cn: 古英语 tol 简短朴素，至今仍指任何帮着干活的东西。

normal.en: Toolbox and toolkit add box and kit, and both mean a container plus what is in it.
normal.cn: toolbox 与 toolkit 分别加 box 与 kit，都表示容器及其中的东西。

normal.en: A tool for doing something is the abstract sense, and for signals it.
normal.cn: a tool for doing something 是抽象义，介词 for 明确标示。

normal.en: Power tools are driven by motors, and the modifier tells you the power source.
normal.cn: power tools 由电机驱动，修饰语说明动力来源。

normal.en: Software tools borrow the plain word because a good program feels like a well-kept hammer.
normal.cn: 软件工具借用这个朴素的词，因为一个好程序像一把保养良好的锤子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching without looking for the hammer that is always in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不看就伸向那柄永远放在原处的锤子。

abstract.en: Think of a simple blade that turns a difficult job into an easy one.
abstract.cn: 想一件简单的刃具，把难活变成易活。

abstract.en: A tool is a hand made harder, longer, or sharper by design.
abstract.cn: 工具是被设计得更硬、更长或更锐利的手。

examples.en: Please put the tools back in the box when you finish.
examples.cn: 做完以后请把工具放回箱子里。

examples.en: Statistics are a tool, not an answer in themselves.
examples.cn: 统计是一种工具，本身不是答案。

examples.en: The workshop was tooled for bicycle frames only.
examples.cn: 那家车间只配备了生产自行车车架的工装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图」——做工程先看图纸，再动手拿工具。

root: 古英语 tol（器具、工具），日耳曼语同源词干 tolam；更早来源不确定。含义由实物器具扩展到抽象手段，二十世纪又扩展到软件工具。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the object in the hand, then reaches for means, for people used by others, for the cutting edge of a machine, and finally for the programs and the verb senses that grew from the same plain word.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从手中的器物写起，继而伸向手段、被利用的人、机床的刃口，最后是同一个朴素词形长出的软件与动词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn handle in the hand that makes work possible.
core.cn: 核心意象：手中被磨旧的握柄，使工作得以完成。

branches.en: The object in the hand and the cutting part of a machine.
branches.cn: 手中之物与机床的刃口。

branches.en: Means, software functions, and command-line programs.
branches.cn: 手段、软件功能与命令行程序。

branches.en: A person treated as an instrument.
The verb of shaping and of equipping.
branches.cn: 表示成形与配备的动词用法。

branches.en: The slang verb for driving.

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic stem with almost no affixes; its growth is by compounding with box, kit, and bar.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的日耳曼语词干，几乎不带词缀，其扩展主要靠与 box、kit、bar 等合成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for the word itself; the Latin entries below belong to borrowed relatives such as instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 本词本身没有拉丁语来源；下列拉丁词条属于 instrument 一类借入的亲属词。

items.exampleCN: 古英语形式只有一个 l。

items.example: Tools is the plural.

items.example: Tooling can mean the tools of a plant.

items.meaning: a set of things for one purpose
items.example: Toolkit is often used figuratively.
Toolbar names the strip of buttons on a screen.

items.example: Power tools replaced many hand tools.
items.exampleCN: 电动工具取代了许多手工工具。

definition_zh: 牙；牙齿；齿状物；（齿轮的）齿
definition_en: one of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting and chewing, or a pointed part shaped like one
core_image: 一排白牙咬住硬纸的边角，发出清脆的一声
scene: 灯下照着镜子里张开的口，牙刷停在最后一颗臼齿上。He brushed each tooth slowly, counting them as he went.
sceneCN: 这里 tooth 就是嘴里的「牙齿」（第 1 个义项：口腔中用于咀嚼的坚硬白色器官）；句意为他把每颗牙慢慢刷过去，边刷边数。画面里有镜子、牙刷与张口的动作。

pos.zh: 名词：齿状物；（齿轮等的）齿

derivatives.zh: 不规则复数形式，义为「牙齿（复数）」
加 -less 构成，义为「无牙的；不起作用的」
加 -y 构成，义为「露齿的；牙齿显眼的」
与 ache 合成，义为「牙痛」

senses.title: The white part in the mouth
senses.definition: one of the hard calcified structures set in the jaws and used for biting and chewing
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在上颌与下颌中的坚硬钙化结构，用于咬与咀嚼
senses.example: The dentist found a small crack in the back tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在后面一颗牙上发现了一条小裂缝。
senses.why: The word is inherited from Old English toth, with a Germanic plural that changes the vowel to teeth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词继承自古英语 toth，其日耳曼语的复数通过元音变化成 teeth。

senses.title: A pointed part of a tool
senses.definition: a projecting part on a comb, a saw, a gear, or a zip
senses.definitionCN: 梳子、锯、齿轮或拉链上凸出的部件
senses.example: One tooth of the zip was bent out of line.
senses.exampleCN: 拉链上有一个齿歪出了线。
senses.why: A comb or a saw works exactly as the mouth does, gripping or cutting with small hard points, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 梳子或锯的工作方式与嘴相同，都是用小而硬的尖端去抓或切，于是同一个词就沿用了。

senses.title: A liking for a kind of food
senses.definition: in informal speech, a liking for a particular kind of food or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某种食物或活动的偏好
senses.example: She has a sweet tooth and never refuses pudding.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱吃甜食，从不拒绝布丁。
senses.why: A craving feels like something in the mouth that wants to bite, so the phrase gives appetite a tooth of its own.
senses.whyCN: 馋意就像嘴里有个想咬东西的部件，于是这个说法也给食欲安上了一颗牙。

senses.title: A tooth in phrases of retaliation
senses.definition: used in the old legal phrase an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 用于「以眼还眼、以牙还牙」这一古老法律短语中
senses.example: The old code demanded a tooth for a tooth, but the new one asks for payment.
senses.exampleCN: 旧律条要求以牙还牙，新法典只要求赔偿。
senses.why: The law of equal revenge names the injured part itself, so losing a tooth is repaid by a tooth.
senses.whyCN: 对等报复的律条直接点出受伤的部位，所以失去一颗牙就以一颗牙偿还。

senses.title: The hard surface that does work
senses.definition: the part of something that grips, cuts, or bites down
senses.definitionCN: 某物中起抓握、切割或咬合作用的部位
senses.example: The clamp has worn teeth that no longer hold the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 夹具的齿磨平了，再也夹不住管子。
senses.why: The point that bites down is the part that does the work, so the word spreads to any gripping surface.
senses.whyCN: 真正用力的是那个咬下去的点，于是这个词扩展到任何起抓握作用的面。

senses.title: Age shown by the teeth
senses.definition: used in phrases that judge age from the state of the teeth, as with horses
senses.definitionCN: 用于按牙齿状况判断年龄的短语，如对马
senses.example: Judging by the tooth, the horse is older than the seller says.
senses.exampleCN: 从牙齿看，这匹马比卖主说的年纪大。
senses.why: Teeth wear in a fixed order, so a farmer reads age in them the way one reads a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿按固定次序磨损，农人看牙如同看日历一样读出年龄。

senses.title: A child growing a tooth
senses.definition: the emergence of a first tooth in a baby
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿第一颗牙长出
senses.example: The baby cut her first tooth at seven months and chewed everything after that.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子七个月时出了第一颗牙，此后什么都想咬。
senses.why: The first tooth is the child's first tool, so cutting it marks the start of eating solid food.
senses.whyCN: 第一颗牙是孩子拥有的第一件工具，它长出来便标志着开始吃固体食物。

senses.title: The unpleasantness of a task
senses.definition: used in the phrase get one's teeth into to mean dealing with hard work properly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get one's teeth into，表示认真对付难事
senses.example: The new project finally gave her something to get her teeth into.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新项目终于让她有了一件可以狠下功夫的事。
senses.why: Hard work is treated as food that needs biting, so sinking the teeth in means committing fully.
senses.whyCN: 难事被当作需要咬住的食物，所以把牙扎进去就是全力投入。

intro.en: Tooth is one of the oldest words in English, from Old English toth, with relatives in every Germanic language and a very old Indo-European root behind them.
intro.cn: tooth 是英语最古老的词之一，来自古英语 toth，在所有日耳曼语中都有亲属词，其背后还有一个非常古老的印欧词根。

items.en: Toth names the biting organ, and the plural tech changes the vowel, a pattern still kept in teeth.
items.cn: 古英语 toth 指咬噬器官，复数 tech 通过元音变化构成，这一模式至今保存在 teeth 里。

items.en: Old Norse tenn, Old High German zan, and Gothic tunthus all trace back to one Germanic stem.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan 与哥特语 tunthus 都可上溯到同一个日耳曼语词干。

items.en: The Latin dens and the Greek odous belong to the same very old Indo-European family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dens 与希腊语 odous 属于同一个非常古老的印欧语族。

items.en: The spelling moves through toth and tothe, and the modern form loses the final vowel sound.
items.cn: 拼写经历 toth 与 tothe 等形态，现代形式丢掉了末尾的元音。

items.en: The word extends early to pointed parts of tools, since a saw tooth bites wood as a tooth bites bread.
items.cn: 这个词很早扩展到工具的尖齿，因为锯齿咬木头正如牙齿咬面包。

items.en: Expressions like sweet tooth and a tooth for a tooth fix the word in proverb and in idiom.
items.cn: sweet tooth 与 a tooth for a tooth 这类说法把这个词固定在谚语与习语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on the word, while the near-meaning group gathers the parts and products of the mouth.
note.cn: 形近组收集由本词构成的复合词与派生词，近义组则汇集口腔部位及相关物。

entries.definition: the irregular plural of tooth
without teeth, or without real power
pain in a tooth
a small enclosed space or stall
entries.definitionCN: 小间；摊位，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the firm pink flesh around the teeth
either of the two bones that hold the teeth
a long sharp tooth of an animal
a long pointed tooth that grows outside the mouth

normalIntro.en: These memories use the irregular plural, the compounds with ache and brush, and the tool sense that grew from biting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用不规则复数、与 ache 和 brush 等构成的搭配，以及由「咬」生长出的工具义。

normal.en: The plural is teeth, not tooths, and the vowel change is the same one in foot and feet.
normal.cn: 复数是 teeth 而不是 tooths，这个元音变化与 foot 变 feet 相同。

normal.en: Toothache adds ache to tooth, and the compound is written as one word.
normal.cn: toothache 由 tooth 加 ache，写成一体。

normal.en: A sweet tooth is an appetite for sugar, and the phrase treats the liking as a body part.
normal.cn: a sweet tooth 指爱吃甜食，这个说法把偏好当作一个身体部件。

normal.en: A tooth for a tooth is the oldest legal formula the word appears in.
normal.cn: a tooth for a tooth 是这个词出现的最古老法律套语。

normal.en: A saw has teeth because it bites wood, which is why tools borrow the word.
normal.cn: 锯有齿是因为它咬木头，工具正是因此借用了这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hard white ridge flashing behind a laugh and then gone.
abstract.cn: 想象笑时露出一道坚白的棱，随即又消失。

abstract.en: Think of gears meshing, each ridge falling into the gap of the next wheel.
abstract.cn: 想齿轮咬合，每个齿落进另一个轮的凹槽。

abstract.en: A tooth is the only part of the body you see being used as a tool every day.
abstract.cn: 牙齿是身体里唯一每天当工具用的部件。

examples.en: The child lost a front tooth and laughed at the gap.
examples.cn: 孩子掉了一颗门牙，对着那个缺口笑。

examples.en: Two teeth on the large gear are worn away.
examples.cn: 大齿轮上有两个齿已经磨损。

examples.en: He has a sweet tooth and keeps chocolate in his desk.
examples.cn: 他爱吃甜食，抽屉里总放着巧克力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凸」——牙是嘴里最硬、最凸出的那一排。

root: 古英语 toth（复数 tech）→ 现代 tooth（复数 teeth）。日耳曼语同源词有古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan；更远处与拉丁语 dens、希腊语 odous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the biting organ, follows the same shape into combs, saws, and gears, and then collects the idioms in which a tooth stands for appetite, for revenge, and for age.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从咬噬器官写起，再顺着同一形状走入梳、锯与齿轮，然后汇集那些用「牙」表示食欲、报复与年龄的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard white ridge made for biting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排为咬合而生的坚硬白棱。

branches.en: The tooth itself and the cutting of a first tooth.
branches.cn: 牙齿本身与第一颗牙的长出。

branches.en: Pointed parts that grip or cut.
branches.cn: 起抓握或切割作用的尖部。

branches.en: Liking for a kind of food.
The old law of equal revenge.
State of the teeth as age, and hard work as biting.
branches.cn: 以牙齿状况示年龄，以咬喻硬功夫。

intro.en: The word is a short inherited stem, so its family grows by vowel change, -less, -y, and compounds with ache and brush.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的继承词干，其词族靠元音变化、-less、-y 以及与 ache、brush 等的合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give dens and its derivatives, the other branch of the same very old family.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出 dens 及其派生词，那是同一古老族系的另一支。

items.example: The stem is unchanged since Old English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干自古英语以来没有变化。

items.example: The Old English form ends in th.
items.exampleCN: 古英语形式以 th 结尾。

items.example: Feet and teeth share the same plural pattern.
items.exampleCN: feet 与 teeth 的复数模式相同。

items.example: Toothless means without teeth.
Toothy describes a wide smile.
Toothache is pain in a tooth.

items.meaning: a brush for a stated use
items.example: A toothbrush is for the teeth.
Toothpaste is used with the brush.
Sweet tooth names a liking for sugar.

definition_zh: 顶部；顶端；盖子；首位；上衣；最上面的；顶部的；超过
definition_en: the highest part or point of something, or the best position, or the covering of a container
core_image: 一只手扶住梯子最上面那一级，脚下是整片屋顶
scene: 爬完最后一节梯子，屋顶就在眼前，风比街上大得多。From the top of the hill you can see the whole harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 top 是「顶部、最高处」（第 1 个义项：物体的最高部分）；句意为从山顶上你能看到整个港湾。画面里有梯子顶端的横档、屋顶与远处的港湾。

pos.zh: 形容词：最上面的；最高的；顶尖的

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「顶部（复数）」，口语中也可作形容词「顶尖的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「（食物上的）浇头；配料」
加 -less 构成，义为「无顶的；无上装的」
加最高级 -most 构成，义为「最上的；最高的」

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the highest point or part of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最高处或最高部分
senses.example: A small flag was fixed to the top of the pole.
senses.exampleCN: 杆子的顶端系着一面小旗。
senses.why: The plain physical sense is the base from which lid, rank, and verb all later develop.
senses.whyCN: 这个最朴素的物理义项，是后来盖子、名次与动词各项含义所由发展的基础。

senses.title: A lid or cover
senses.definition: the cover of a container or bottle
senses.definitionCN: 容器或瓶子的封盖
senses.example: Screw the top back on before you shake it.
senses.exampleCN: 摇之前先把盖子拧回去。
senses.why: A lid closes a vessel at its top, so the word for the highest part names the cover too.
senses.whyCN: 盖子在容器顶端封口，于是表示最高部分的词也用来指盖子。

senses.title: The best or highest position
senses.definition: the leading place in a group, a list, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在群体、名单或行业中的领先位置
senses.example: She finished the season at the top of the rankings.
senses.exampleCN: 她在赛季结束时排名榜首。
senses.why: A ranking is a vertical list, so the person at the highest point of it is at the top.
senses.whyCN: 排名是一张竖着的名单，位于其最高点的人就在 top。

senses.title: A garment for the upper body
senses.definition: a piece of clothing worn on the upper body
senses.definitionCN: 穿在上身的衣物
senses.example: He put on a clean top and went down to dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他换上一件干净的上衣下楼吃饭。
senses.why: A top is the garment on the upper half of the body, and the word simply reuses the idea of the upper part.
senses.whyCN: top 指穿在上半身的衣物，这个词只是再次动用了「上部」这一概念。

senses.title: The highest in rank
senses.definition: as an adjective, highest in rank, quality, or position
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时指等级、质量或位置最高的
senses.example: The matter is a top priority for the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事是整个部门的头等大事。
senses.why: The adjective is formed from the noun without any ending, which is common for short English words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由名词构成，不加任何词尾，这对英语短词很常见。

senses.title: To be higher than
senses.definition: to be greater in amount or degree than something else
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上高出另者
senses.example: Sales topped two million copies in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 首月销量超过了两百万册。
senses.why: A figure is like a mark on a pole, and to pass above it is to top it.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字像杆上的刻度，越过去就是 top it。

senses.title: To cover the surface of
senses.definition: to put something on the upper surface of food or of a structure
senses.definitionCN: 在食物或结构的上表面加上某物
senses.example: She topped the cake with thin slices of lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她在蛋糕上铺了薄薄的柠檬片。
senses.why: Topping a dish is putting something on its upper surface, and the cooking verb keeps the meaning literal.
senses.whyCN: 给菜加浇头就是在它的上表面放东西，这个烹饪动词保留了字面意义。

senses.title: The head in informal speech
senses.definition: in informal speech, the head or hair on it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指头顶或其上的头发
senses.example: He took his cap off and scratched the top of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他摘下帽子挠了挠头顶。
senses.why: The informal head sense descends from the old word for a tuft of hair on the crown.
senses.whyCN: 口语中的「头顶」义来自那个表示头顶发簇的古词。

senses.title: A spinning toy
senses.definition: a toy that spins on a point, an older sense kept in the word's history
senses.definitionCN: 一种以尖端着地旋转的玩具，是这个词较早的义项
senses.example: The spinning toy is a separate word that happens to share the spelling, and it survives in the modern language only in this narrow use.
senses.exampleCN: 这种旋转玩具有自己的词源，只是恰好同形，今天只在极窄的用法里留存。
senses.why: The toy turns on a single point at its bottom, so the shape of a top on a point links the two words by accident of form.
senses.whyCN: 陀螺以底部的一个尖点旋转，于是「尖顶」之形与它偶然相连，成了同形的两个词。

intro.en: Top is an Old English word for the highest part, and an older separate sense names a spinning top; the two senses were probably never the same word.
intro.cn: top 在古英语中表示最高部分；另一个更早的义项指陀螺，两者很可能从来不是同一个词。

items.en: Top names the summit or the highest point, and is used of hills, trees, and buildings.
items.cn: 古英语 top 指顶巅或最高点，用于山、树与建筑。

items.en: A separate word topp names a tuft of hair on the head, which explains the informal sense of the head.
items.cn: 另有一个词 topp 指头上一簇头发，这解释了口语中「头顶」的义项。

items.en: Old Norse toppr and Old High German zopf all mean a summit or a tuft.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 toppr 与古高地德语 zopf 都表示顶或发簇。

items.en: Middle English applies top to lids and covers, since a lid sits at the top of a vessel.
items.cn: 中古英语把 top 用于盖子，因为盖正位于容器的顶上。

items.en: The verb to top appears in the sixteenth century with the sense of putting something on the upper surface.
items.cn: 动词 top 于十六世纪出现，义为在表面之上放东西。

items.en: The sense of surpassing comes in the seventeenth century, from the idea of going above a mark.
items.cn: 「超过」之义于十七世纪出现，源自越过某个标记的想法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short forms built on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for summit, cover, and ranking.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干构成的短形式，近义组则汇集表示顶部、盖子与名次的词。

the very highest
the flat upper surface of a table
a faucet, or a light knock
